test.description: VSEPR Theory, Structure and Bond Angle of Molecules

en.explanation:
1. Analysis of $S_3^{2-}$

  • Structure: The central sulfur atom is bonded to two other sulfur atoms.

  • Electron Pairs: The central atom has 2 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs.

  • Steric Number: $2 \text{ (bond pairs)} + 2 \text{ (lone pairs)} = 4$.

  • Hybridization: $sp^3$.

  • Shape: The expected tetrahedral geometry is distorted by the two lone pairs, resulting in a bent or V-shaped (angular) shape.

2. Analysis of $I_3^{-}$

  • Structure: The central iodine atom is bonded to two other iodine atoms via single bonds.

  • Electron Pairs: The central atom has 2 bond pairs and 3 lone pairs.

  • Steric Number: $2 + 3 = 5$.

  • Hybridization: $sp^3d$.

  • Shape: The three lone pairs occupy the equatorial positions to minimize repulsion, leaving the atoms in a linear arrangement.

3. Analysis of $N_3^{-}$

  • Structure: The central nitrogen atom is bonded to two other nitrogen atoms (drawn in the video with a triple bond to one nitrogen and a single bond to the other).

  • Electron Pairs: The central nitrogen has 2 sigma bond pairs and 0 lone pairs.

  • Steric Number: $2$.

  • Hybridization: $sp$.

  • Shape: Because there are no lone pairs on the central atom to distort the bonds, the shape is strictly linear.

Conclusion

Since $S_3^{2-}$ is the only molecule analyzed that exhibits an angular geometry, the correct answer is Option (A).

en.content: In which of the following species maximum atom can lie in same plane?
en.explanation:
We have to analyze the structure and geometry of each species and then determine the maximum number of atoms that can lie in the same plane.

A. $\mathrm{XeF}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$

It has a trigonal bipyramidal geometry. Here, the maximum number of atoms in the same plane is $4(\mathrm{Xe}, \mathrm{F}, \mathrm{F}$, and O$)$.

B. $\mathrm{PCl}_5$

It also has a trigonal bipyramidal structure; here, the maximum number of atoms is 4 (P and 3Cl).

C. $\mathrm{AsH}_4{ }^{+}$

It has a tetrahedral shape; here, the coplanar atoms are 3 ( As and 2H atoms).

D. $\mathrm{XeF}_4$

$\mathrm{XeF}_4$ has a square planar structure, where 5 atoms lie in the same plane ( Xe and 4 F atoms).

Since $\mathrm{XeF}_4$ has the maximum coplanar atoms (5). Therefore, our answer is D.

en.content: The geometrical arrangement of orbitals and shape of $I_3^-$ are respectively :
en.explanation:
First, we have to find the hybridization of $I_3^-$ molecule.

$$H = \frac{1}{2}(V + M - C + A)$$

Here, $V$ = number of the valence electrons in the atom,

$M$ = number of the monovalent atoms bonded to the central atom,

$C$ = the charge on the cation

$A$ = the charge on the anion

Applying this we get, $$H = (7+2+1)/2 = 10/2 = 5$$

So, the hybridization is $sp^3$ implies it has a Trigonal bipyramidal geometry

Regarding the shape, the three lone pairs occupy the equatorial positions to minimize repulsion. Therefore, it has a linear shape.

Answer : A

en.content:
How many of the following species are planar?

$$ \mathrm{PCl}_3, \mathrm{NH}_2^{-}, \mathrm{BrF}_3, \mathrm{XeO}_2 \mathrm{~F}_2, \mathrm{XeF}_4, \mathrm{SiO}_2, \mathrm{CO}_2, \mathrm{SF}_4 $$
en.explanation:
1. $\mathrm{PCl}_3$: Phosphorus has 5 valence electrons. It forms 3 bond pairs with chlorine atoms and has 1 lone pair. The steric number is 4 ($sp^3$ hybridized), giving it a trigonal pyramidal shape. Since the atoms do not lie in one plane, it is non-planar.

  2. $\mathrm{NH}_2^{-}$: Nitrogen has 5 valence electrons, plus 1 extra electron from the negative charge, making 6. It forms 2 bond pairs with hydrogen atoms and has 2 lone pairs. The shape is bent (V-shaped). Because any triatomic molecule or ion has its three nuclei lying in a single plane, it is planar.

  3. $\mathrm{BrF}_3$: Bromine has 7 valence electrons. It forms 3 bond pairs with fluorine atoms and has 2 lone pairs ($sp^3d$ hybridized). To minimize repulsion, the lone pairs occupy equatorial positions, resulting in a T-shaped geometry. All four atoms lie in a single plane, so it is planar.

  4. $\mathrm{XeO}_2\mathrm{F}_2$: Xenon has 8 valence electrons. It forms 2 double bonds with oxygen and 2 single bonds with fluorine, leaving 1 lone pair ($sp^3d$ hybridized). This forms a seesaw shape, which is non-planar.

  5. $\mathrm{XeF}_4$: Xenon forms 4 bond pairs with fluorine atoms and has 2 lone pairs ($sp^3d^2$ hybridized). The lone pairs sit opposite each other in axial positions, leaving the four fluorine atoms arranged around xenon in a single plane. This gives a square planar shape, so it is planar.

  6. $\mathrm{SiO}_2$: Silicon dioxide exists as a continuous three-dimensional covalent network solid where each silicon atom is tetrahedrally linked to four oxygen atoms. Therefore, it is non-planar.

  7. $\mathrm{CO}_2$: Carbon forms 2 double bonds with oxygen atoms and has no lone pairs ($sp$ hybridized). The geometry is linear, meaning all three atoms lie on a straight line, so it is planar.

  8. $\mathrm{SF}_4$: Sulfur has 6 valence electrons, forming 4 bond pairs and keeping 1 lone pair ($sp^3d$ hybridized). This gives a seesaw shape, which is non-planar.

The planar species among the given options are $\mathrm{NH}_2^{-}$, $\mathrm{BrF}_3$, $\mathrm{XeF}_4$, and $\mathrm{CO}_2$.

Out of the given 8 species, 4 are planar.

en.content:
Number of molecules or ions which has/have any bond angle of $120^{\circ}$ is

$$ \stackrel{-}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}_3, \stackrel{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}_3, \mathrm{NH}_3, \mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}, \mathrm{BCl}_3, \mathrm{PCl}_5 $$
en.explanation:
The species which have at least one bond angle of $120^\circ$ are:

$$\overset{+}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}_3,\ \mathrm{CO}_3^{2-},\ \mathrm{BCl}_3,\ \mathrm{PCl}_5$$

Using VSEPR idea:

  • $\overset{-}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}_3$ has $3$ bond pairs and $1$ lone pair on carbon.

    Its shape is pyramidal, similar to $\mathrm{NH}_3$, so the bond angle is not $120^\circ$.

  • $\overset{+}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}_3$ has $3$ bond pairs and no lone pair on carbon.

    It is trigonal planar, so:

    $$\angle \mathrm{HCH}=120^\circ$$

  • $\mathrm{NH}_3$ has $3$ bond pairs and $1$ lone pair on nitrogen.

    It is pyramidal with bond angle about $107^\circ$, not $120^\circ$.

  • $\mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}$ is trigonal planar around carbon, so:

    $$\angle \mathrm{OCO}=120^\circ$$

  • $\mathrm{BCl}_3$ is trigonal planar, so:

    $$\angle \mathrm{ClBCl}=120^\circ$$

  • $\mathrm{PCl}_5$ has trigonal bipyramidal geometry.

    The angle between two equatorial chlorine atoms is:

    $$120^\circ$$

So, the number of species having any bond angle of $120^\circ$ is

$$\boxed{4}$$
